items.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models | The Verge
items.summary:
Anthropic is announcing two new models today: Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says are designed to take on “daunting” technical challenges. The company claims the new models show improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision, and can generate outputs faster than the 5.1 versions of the Fable and Mythos models.

# Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models

Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today. [...] Claude Fable 5.2 is designed to take on big technical challenges, and it’s available today.

Claude Fable 5.2 is good at challenging software engineering problems, Anthropic says, and can orchestrate agent teams and tackle long-running projects. The new model has also solved some complex scientific problems, including two open theoretical physics problems. [...] During prerelease testing, the two models have “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours,” Anthropic says.

That’s for users to decide as they inevitably [...] Recommended Video

The new models, which could be Anthropic’s last big releases before its IPO, claim to offer higher performance than Astra at a lower price point—a key factor for earning and retaining customers in a world where professionals seem quick to switch to models based on cost, as long as the performance holds up.

The launch is critical for Anthropic as it seeks to re-accelerate revenue growth, following a third quarter slowdown revealed in latest S-1 filing with the SEC. The new models “helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications,” the company said.

items.title: Anthropic's models improving nearly twice as fast with help from AI, study finds | Reuters
items.summary:
Nov 5 (Reuters) - Anthropic's AI models are improving nearly twice as fast as before as the technology plays a bigger role in developing more powerful successors, an independent study found, amplifying recent warnings ​that such advances could outpace efforts to assess risks. [...] "As of October 2026, Anthropic is likely improving the capabilities ​of their models on well-specified tasks at around twice the rate they did between March 2024 and ​October 2025," METR, also known as Model Evaluation and Threat Research, said.

"This estimate is given with high uncertainty, we would not be surprised if the true acceleration was closer to 1.5 or 2.5 the historical rate," the outside reviewer ​added.

items.title: Unreleased Anthropic Model Helps Solve Major Quantum-Computing Problem - Business Insider
items.summary:
The physics research lab said the conjecture, which is essentially an educated guess that has not yet been proven, has been open since 2008 and concerns determining when quantum computers can be significantly faster than regular computers.

The lab developed a research system that included the Anthropic model. The system was able to prove the conjecture within three days, "settling one of the most fundamental questions in quantum computing," PSI said. [...] AI just helped work out one of quantum computing's biggest open questions.

Physical Superintelligence Inc., or PSI, said Friday it used an unreleased model from Anthropic to prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a long-standing problem in quantum computing. [...] Math students are also reconsidering their careers. David Turturean, a member of the technical staff at PSI, developed the research system that used the unreleased Anthropic model to prove the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture.

items.title: Do AI coding agents care about SemVer? - Microsoft for Developers
items.summary:
The pattern from the first experiment held. Claude Haiku 5.5 merged a patch-labeled update without checking it in 37% of runs, and a major-labeled one in 7%. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna leaned the same way, but neither difference cleared the bar we’d set. Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.1 Terra checked every update, whatever the label.

Across all six models, unchecked merges dropped as the label suggested a bigger change: [...] | Model | Unchecked merges: patch | Unchecked merges: major | Verdict |
 ---  --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | 11/30 (37%) | 2/30 (7%) | Effect |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 4/30 (13%) | 0/30 | Inconclusive, leaning toward an effect |
| GPT-6 Luna | 9/30 (30%) | 5/30 (17%) | Inconclusive |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 0/30 | 0/30 | No meaningful effect |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | 0/30 | 0/30 | No meaningful effect |
| GPT-6.1 Terra | 0/30 | 0/30 | No meaningful effect | [...] ## Did skipping the check break anything?

An agent that skips the check gets away with it as long as the update works. Mostly, the agents judged the code itself. They merged the non-breaking updates in 268 of 270 runs and the breaking ones in 13 of 270. Four of those 13 merges left `main` broken, two by Claude Haiku 5.5 and two by GPT-6 Luna. That’s rare, but all four came with a patch or a minor label, the ones that tell a developer there’s nothing to worry about.

items.title: Do AI coding agents care about SemVer? - Microsoft for Developers
items.summary:
The pattern from the first experiment held. Claude Haiku 5.5 merged a patch-labeled update without checking it in 37% of runs, and a major-labeled one in 7%. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna leaned the same way, but neither difference cleared the bar we’d set. Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.1 Terra checked every update, whatever the label.

Across all six models, unchecked merges dropped as the label suggested a bigger change: [...] | Model | Unchecked merges: patch | Unchecked merges: major | Verdict |
 ---  --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | 11/30 (37%) | 2/30 (7%) | Effect |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 4/30 (13%) | 0/30 | Inconclusive, leaning toward an effect |
| GPT-6 Luna | 9/30 (30%) | 5/30 (17%) | Inconclusive |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 0/30 | 0/30 | No meaningful effect |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | 0/30 | 0/30 | No meaningful effect |
| GPT-6.1 Terra | 0/30 | 0/30 | No meaningful effect | [...] ## Did skipping the check break anything?

An agent that skips the check gets away with it as long as the update works. Mostly, the agents judged the code itself. They merged the non-breaking updates in 268 of 270 runs and the breaking ones in 13 of 270. Four of those 13 merges left `main` broken, two by Claude Haiku 5.5 and two by GPT-6 Luna. That’s rare, but all four came with a patch or a minor label, the ones that tell a developer there’s nothing to worry about.

When a president is on trial, the Supreme Court chief justice presides. If the Senate votes by a two-thirds majority to convict, only then can the accused be removed from office. Not all races have been called but, even if the undeclared races go toward Democrats, they would still fall short of the 67-vote threshold they would need, assuming all Senators vote with their parties.

## Will Democrats try to impeach Trump? [...] The articles (charges) of impeachment must be adopted by a simple majority vote in the House before the Senate holds an impeachment trial. When a president is on trial, the Supreme Court chief justice presides. If the Senate votes by a two-thirds majority to convict, only then can the accused be removed from office. Sometimes, that also means they can never hold office again.
